content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated OOMs in decode-stream cluster us-west-2 / pool gpu-pool-3 — 42% of decode pods reporting CUDA OOMs in last 3m. Pager sent to oncall.

maria-ops: paging @ajay-oncall — we're getting a steady stream of OOMs + pod restarts, customer requests dropping. oncall please ack.

ajay-oncall: ACK. I'm pulling logs now. ... attaching quick grep output
ajay-oncall: ```
2026-03-17T14:21:03Z decode: request_id=abc123 client=api-foo max_tokens=1000000 streaming=true
2026-03-17T14:21:03Z decode: allocate cuda: OOM at 11.2GB used
2026-03-17T14:21:04Z pod kubelet: container restart backoff
``` 

ajay-oncall: looks like a runaway generation — many requests with huge max_tokens (1e6) slipped through. suspect a client-side bug or a config mismatch in router defaults.

lexi-runtime: can we hotpatch the router policy to enforce a server-side cap? If we set per-request token limit to 2048 and disable streaming for suspicious route, should reduce KV cache growth and OOMs.

ajay-oncall: doing that now. Applying route-level enforcement + throttle.
ajay-oncall: ```bash
# quick mitigation
curl -X POST "https://router.internal/api/rules" -d '{"route":"/v1/decode","max_tokens":2048,"streaming":false}'
kubectl drain pod/gpu-decode-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl scale deploy/gpu-decode --replicas=6
```

maria-ops: I'm scaling up as well, bumping capacity to absorb backlog. also adding a short-lived global rate limit 20rps per tenant.

jordan-cs: customer impact? CS needs numbers to notify customers.

ajay-oncall: early estimate: ~2.3k requests dropped or errored in the last 10m, affecting two tenants (tenant:acme, tenant:beta-inc). I've opened ticket RH-4217 for ACME (high priority).

jordan-cs: thanks — I'll draft a customer note: brief, say we detected anomalous token caps causing request storms, mitigations applied, working on permanent fix.

lexi-runtime: next steps: 1) keep server cap for 24h 2) add routing alert for per-request token > 100k 3) coordinate with reseller to patch client SDK default that sets max_tokens to infinity on retries 4) run postmortem once stable.

ajay-oncall: handing off to @lexi-runtime for next shift. I'll leave the temporary rate limits and router rule in place. linking logs + dump in #incidents-artifacts.

lexi-runtime: Taking over. I'll also run a KV cache eviction across nodes and check for memory fragmentation. ETA 15m.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-17/gpu-decode-unbounded -> mitigated: router cap applied, pod restarts decreased to <2/min. Severity reduced to P2. Playbook run: enforced limits, scaled pool, opened CS ticket.

maria-ops: thanks team. after stabilization please file a concise blameless postmortem and add the client SDK in failing clients list.

ajay-oncall: one last note — we should add validation in API gateway to reject max_tokens > 100k; will file a follow-up PR.

lexi-runtime: confirmed stable; moving to monitoring. :white_check_mark:
